boundary_conditions: This principle applies specifically to scenarios where the refractive interface is dynamic and the viewing angles are limited to a sequence of images captured through this changing medium, requiring the surface model to support temporal variation.

payload.discussion: Sequential approaches often fail because errors in estimating the surface shape propagate directly into the scene reconstruction, creating artifacts that are indistinguishable from actual scene features. By optimizing both components jointly, the system can leverage constraints from the entire image sequence to disambiguate whether a visual feature arises from surface curvature or scene geometry.
payload.evidence: The text describes optimizing rendered images to match input images to reconstruct both the boundary surface shape and the NeRF of the target scene simultaneously, implying that solving for one without the other yields insufficient accuracy due to the coupling of refraction and scene content.

work_version_records.abstract: : In this study, we propose a method to simultaneously reconstruct the NeRF of a scene behind a refractive surface and the shape of the refractive surface itself from a sequence of distorted images captured through dynamically changing surfaces such as water. To achieve this, we introduce a shape model capable of representing dynamic boundary surfaces. By performing ray tracing on the captured images using this model, it becomes possible to render accurate images even in scenes involving refraction. Furthermore, by optimizing the rendered images to match the input images, both the boundary surface shape and the NeRF of the target scene can be reconstructed simultaneously.
